concept.name: Gradient boosting
concept.definition: Boosting that adds weak learners fitted to the negative gradient of a differentiable loss with respect to current predictions.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Compute current predictions and loss gradients, fit a small tree to those gradients, scale it by a learning rate, and add it to the model.
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: A regression tree fitted to residual-like gradients is multiplied by 0.05 and added as iteration 20.
